chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Abu Ahmad from 'Amr, the master of al-Karabis, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who manumitted his slave on condition that the inheritance would be his, he raised that matter to Ali (peace be upon him), who annulled his condition and said, 'The condition of God is prior to your condition.'

key_terms.شرط الله: The condition of God (divine default ruling)
key_terms.مكاتبة: Manumission contract where a slave pays a lump sum or installments for freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master conditions that he inherits his mukatab slave?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *tarjih* (preference) by prioritizing the general divine decree of inheritance over the specific contractual stipulation of the master. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that *mukatabah* conditions cannot override the fixed shares (*furud*) prescribed in the Quran, ensuring the slave retains their rightful inheritance upon manumission.
